newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says CanWest ruling not general policy.
newsitem.headline: Australia says CanWest ruling not general policy.

text.p: The Australian government's decision to order Canada's CanWest Global Communications Corp to cut its economic stake in the Ten television network did not have any implications for media policy or foreign investment policy generally, Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday.
"I don't think it has any implications other than for the case that was actually decided," Costello told a news conference.

Costello said Australia had a liberal foreign investment regime generally, but that in certain sectors like the media, banking and telecommunications the government judged it was in the national interest not to allow high levels of foreign ownership.
Costello ruled last month that CanWest must cut its economic stake in Ten from 76 percent to its previously sanctioned level of 57.5 percent.
He said most would agree that 76 percent foreign ownership of a television network was too high and that 57.5 percent could not be considered a low level.
